It is as though those who do not perform the deeds of the Hereafter, do not strive in God's cause, and do not reflect with the reflection of people of religion, and do not seek insight, were like the disabled who cannot use their limbs, and like those whose minds are taken away and who have no insight. This contains a veiled reproach to everyone who is not among the workers of God and not among those who seek insight into the religion of God, and a rebuke for abandoning striving and contemplation although they are capable of both.

It is also read ﴿ulī al-aydī﴾, as a plural of plural. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is ﴿ulī al-ayd﴾, with the yā' dropped and the kasra kept as sufficient. Explaining it as "the ayd" from ta'yid (support) is unsteady and not firmly grounded.

﴿We made them sincere﴾ means: We made them pure. ﴿With a pure quality﴾ means: with a quality that is unmixed and free of impurity. Then He explained it as ﴿the remembrance of the abode﴾, as a witness that the remembrance of the abode is pure, clear, and free of any turbidity. It is also read with an idafa (construct), ﴿bi-khalisati dhikra al-dar﴾, meaning: by what is pure of the remembrance of the abode, so that they do not mix the remembrance of the abode with any other concern; their only concern is the remembrance of the abode and nothing else.

The meaning of ﴿the remembrance of the abode﴾ is: their constant remembrance of the Hereafter, and their forgetting of the worldly life in favour of it. Or it means reminding others of the Hereafter, encouraging them towards it, and making them averse to this world, as is the way and habit of the prophets. It has also been said that ﴿the remembrance of the abode﴾ means the good praise in this world and the true tongue (of praise) that belongs to no one else.

If you ask: what is the meaning of ﴿We made them sincere by a pure quality﴾? I say: its meaning is: We made them sincere because of this quality, and because they belong to its people. Or: We made them sincere by granting them success in it and by showing them kindness in choosing it. The first explanation is supported by the reading of one who reads ﴿bi-khalisatihim﴾ ("by their pure quality").

﴿The chosen ones﴾ means: chosen from among their kind. ﴿Al-akhyar﴾ is the plural of khayr, or of khayyir, with the lightening (of the doubled letter), like ﴿al-amwat﴾ as plural of mayyit or mayt.

and al-Yasa'; it is as if the definite article had entered upon Yasa'. It is also read: wal-Lais'a, as if the definite article had entered upon Lais'a, which is of the pattern fay'al, from al-las' (stinging). And the tanwin in "wa-kullun" is a substitute for the genitive complement that was omitted; its meaning is: and all of them are among the righteous.

This is a kind of remembrance (dhikr), namely the Qur'an, since he had concluded the mention of the prophets. It is one section of the revelation and one of its types, and he wished to mention after it another section, namely the mention of Paradise and its people. [[Mahmud said: "He only said 'This is a remembrance' so that after it he would mention another remembrance, namely the mention of Paradise and its people, just as al-Jahiz says in his books: 'This is one section,' then he begins another section." Ahmad said: Just as the jurist says when he has mentioned the proofs of a question, upon completing the first proof: "This is a second proof, such-and-such," and so on to the end of what is in his mind. It is evidence for this that when he finished mentioning the people of Paradise he said: "This is so. And indeed for the transgressors is an evil place of return," and so mentioned the people of the Fire.]] He said: "This is a remembrance," then said "And indeed for the God-fearing," as al-Jahiz says in his books: "This is one section," then he begins another section, and as a writer says when he has finished a chapter of his book and wishes to begin another: "This, and it was such-and-such." The proof of this is that when he had completed the mention of the people of Paradise and wished to follow it with the mention of the people of the Fire, he said: "This, and indeed for the transgressors."

It was said that its meaning is: "This is honour and a fine mention by which they will be remembered forever." And from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him: "This is the remembrance of those prophets who passed."

﴿Gardens of Eden, whose doors are opened for them﴾. "Gardens of Eden" is definite because of His saying ﴿Gardens of Eden, which the Most Merciful has promised to His servants﴾, and its being in the accusative is because it is an explicative apposition (ʿatf bayan) to "a good place of return." "Opened" (mufattahah) is a circumstantial clause (hal), and the element governing it is the sense of the verb contained in "for the God-fearing" (lil-muttaqin). In "mufattahah" there is a pronoun referring to the gardens, and "the doors" (al-abwab) is a substitute (badal) for that pronoun; its underlying sense is: "opened, they being the doors," like the saying "Zayd was struck on the hand and the leg," which is a substitution of part (badal al-ishtimal).

It was also read as "Gardens of Eden, opened" in the nominative, on the basis that "Gardens of Eden" is the subject (mubtada') and "opened" is its predicate.

Or both are the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "It is Gardens of Eden; they are opened for them." As if the ladies were of equal age, companions of the same age (atrab), because their menstruation occurs at one time, and they were made of one age, because affection between peers is more firm. And it was said: "They are of equal age to their husbands, their ages like theirs."

It was read as *yūʿadūna* (يوعدون, "they are promised") with a *tāʾ* (ت) and also with a *yāʾ* (ي), *liyawmi l-ḥisāb* (ليوم الحساب) "for the Day of Reckoning." *Li-ajli* (لأجل) means "for the sake of" or "on account of": *liyawmi l-ḥisāb* means "for the sake of the Day of Reckoning," as when you say, "This is what you store up for the Day of Reckoning." That is, "for the Day on which every soul will be recompensed for what it has done."

It was read as *yūʿadūna* (يوعدون, "they are promised") with a *tāʾ* (ت) and also with a *yāʾ* (ي), *liyawmi l-ḥisāb* (ليوم الحساب) "for the Day of Reckoning." *Li-ajli* (لأجل) means "for the sake of" or "on account of": *liyawmi l-ḥisāb* means "for the sake of the Day of Reckoning," as when you say, "This is what you store up for the Day of Reckoning." That is, "for the Day on which every soul will be recompensed for what it has done."

This is (the matter), or it is as mentioned: ﴿so wretched is the resting place﴾, like His saying ﴿for them there will be a bed of Hell, and above them coverings of fire﴾. He likened what is beneath them of the Fire to the bedding that a sleeper spreads out. That is: this is scalding water, so let them taste it. Or the punishment is this, so let them taste it, and then he began, saying: ﴿it is scalding water and ghassaq﴾. Or: ﴿this, so let them taste it﴾ is in the same position as ﴿and Me, so fear Me﴾, meaning: let them taste this, so let them taste it. Al-ghassaq, whether with light or heavy pronunciation, is what flows from the pus of the people of the Fire. It is said: "the eye dripped (ghasaqat al-'ayn)" when its tears flowed. It was also said: the hamim (scalding water) burns with its heat, and the ghassaq burns with its cold. It was also said: if a single drop of it were dripped in the East, it would stink up the people of the West, and if a single drop of it were dripped in the West, it would stink up the people of the East. And from al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him: "Al-ghassaq is a punishment that no one knows except Allah, the Exalted."

People concealed obedience to Allah, so He concealed a reward for them, in His saying ﴿no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾. They concealed disobedience, so He concealed a punishment for them. ﴿And other punishments of a similar kind to this one, in severity and dreadfulness, in pairs﴾: kinds. It has been recited as ﴿wa-akharu﴾ (and another), meaning: and another punishment, or another kind of taste.

﴿Azwaj﴾ (pairs) is an adjective of ﴿akhar﴾, since it is permissible for it to be varieties. Or it is an adjective of the three: ﴿hamim﴾, ﴿ghassaq﴾, and ﴿akhar min shaklihi﴾. It has been recited as ﴿min shaklihi﴾ with a kasra, and this is a dialect. [[His saying "and it has been recited min shaklihi with a kasra, and this is a dialect": meaning in the sense of "likeness" (al-shakl bi-ma'na al-mithl). (Ghunaymi)]] As for ﴿al-ghunj﴾ [[His saying "as for al-ghunj, it is with a kasra only": in al-Sihah: al-ghunj and al-ghanj mean shakl (form/likeness), and the girl has been ghunjat and taghannajat, so she is ghunjah. Also in it: al-shakl, with a fatha, means the like, and with a kasra means flirtatious grace; one says "a woman of shakl." (Ghunaymi)]], then it is with a kasra only.

﴿This is a crowd rushing in with you﴾: this is a large crowd that has rushed into the Fire with you, meaning it entered the Fire in your company and alongside you. Al-iqtiham is undertaking hardship and entering into it, and al-qahmah is hardship. This is the report of the speech of the tyrants among themselves, meaning they say this. The intended meaning of "the crowd" is their followers, who rushed into misguidance with them, so they rush into the punishment with them. ﴿No welcome to them﴾: a supplication from them against their followers. One says to whom one prays for: "marhaban" (welcome), meaning: you have come to a spacious land, not a narrow one, or: your land has become spacious for you, a spaciousness. Then "la" (no) is placed before it in an evil supplication.

﴿To them﴾ is an explanation of those against whom the supplication is made. ﴿Indeed they will burn in the Fire﴾ is a reason for their deserving the supplication against them. Similar to it is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾. It was also said: ﴿this is a crowd rushing in with you﴾ is the speech of the keepers (of Hell) to the leaders of the disbelievers, concerning their followers. ﴿No welcome to them, indeed they will burn in the Fire﴾ is the speech of the leaders. It was also said: all of this is the speech of the keepers.

﴿They said﴾, meaning the followers: ﴿Rather, you—no welcome to you! You have brought this upon us﴾. They mean: the supplication you prayed against us, you are more deserving of it. They gave as the reason their saying: ﴿you brought it upon us﴾, and the pronoun refers to the punishment or to its burning. If you ask: what is the meaning of their bringing the punishment upon them? I say: what is brought forward is the evil deed. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning. That is for what your hands have sent forward﴾. But since the leaders were the cause of it through their misleading, and the punishment was their requital for it, it was said: "you brought it forward for us." So the leaders are made the ones who bring forward, and the requital is made the thing brought forward. Thus two metaphors are combined, because the doers are in reality the ones who bring it forward, not their leaders, and the deed is what is brought forward, not its requital.

If you ask: then what of the one who made His saying ﴿no welcome to them﴾ the speech of the keepers, and how does His saying ﴿rather, you—no welcome to you﴾ fit with it, when the addressees, namely their leaders, did not speak in a way that would be a reply to them? I say: it is as if it were said: this which the keepers prayed against us, you, O leaders, are more deserving of it than we are, because of your misleading us and your causing what we are in of punishment. This is sound, as when a people beautify some wrongdoing for another people, who then commit it, and it is said to those who beautified it: "May Allah disgrace these people! How evil is their deed!" Then the one who beautified it says to those who beautified it: "Rather, you are more deserving of disgrace than we are. Were it not for you, we would not have committed that."

They said, the followers also: ﴿so increase him in punishment, doubled﴾, meaning multiplied, and its meaning: having double. Similar to it is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, these are the ones who misled us, so give them a double punishment﴾. It is that He adds to his punishment the like of it, so that it becomes two punishments, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment﴾. [[His saying, Exalted is He: "They said: Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, increase him in punishment, doubled," and He said in another place: "Give them double the punishment, and curse them with a great curse," and the story is one. Ahmad said: in this there is evidence that the two doubles are two of one thing, contrary to whoever said otherwise, because in one place He said ﴿increase him in punishment, doubled﴾, and the intended meaning is: the like of his punishment, so they become two punishments. And in two places He said ﴿doubled﴾, and the intended meaning is: having two punishments.]] It was reported in the exegesis, "a punishment, doubled": snakes and serpents. This is (the matter), or it is as mentioned: ﴿so wretched is the resting place﴾, like His saying ﴿for them there will be a bed of Hell, and above them coverings of fire﴾. He likened what is beneath them of the Fire to the bedding that a sleeper spreads out. That is: this is scalding water, so let them taste it. Or the punishment is this, so let them taste it, and then he began, saying: ﴿it is scalding water and ghassaq﴾. Or: ﴿this, so let them taste it﴾ is in the same position as ﴿and Me, so fear Me﴾, meaning: let them taste this, so let them taste it. Al-ghassaq, whether with light or heavy pronunciation, is what flows from the pus of the people of the Fire. It is said: "the eye dripped (ghasaqat al-'ayn)" when its tears flowed. It was also said: the hamim (scalding water) burns with its heat, and the ghassaq burns with its cold. It was also said: if a single drop of it were dripped in the East, it would stink up the people of the West, and if a single drop of it were dripped in the West, it would stink up the people of the East. And from al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him: "Al-ghassaq is a punishment that no one knows except Allah, the Exalted."

People concealed obedience to Allah, so He concealed a reward for them, in His saying ﴿no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾. They concealed disobedience, so He concealed a punishment for them. ﴿And other punishments of a similar kind to this one, in severity and dreadfulness, in pairs﴾: kinds. It has been recited as ﴿wa-akharu﴾ (and another), meaning: and another punishment, or another kind of taste.

﴿Azwaj﴾ (pairs) is an adjective of ﴿akhar﴾, since it is permissible for it to be varieties. Or it is an adjective of the three: ﴿hamim﴾, ﴿ghassaq﴾, and ﴿akhar min shaklihi﴾. It has been recited as ﴿min shaklihi﴾ with a kasra, and this is a dialect. [[His saying "and it has been recited min shaklihi with a kasra, and this is a dialect": meaning in the sense of "likeness" (al-shakl bi-ma'na al-mithl). (Ghunaymi)]] As for ﴿al-ghunj﴾ [[His saying "as for al-ghunj, it is with a kasra only": in al-Sihah: al-ghunj and al-ghanj mean shakl (form/likeness), and the girl has been ghunjat and taghannajat, so she is ghunjah. Also in it: al-shakl, with a fatha, means the like, and with a kasra means flirtatious grace; one says "a woman of shakl." (Ghunaymi)]], then it is with a kasra only.

﴿This is a crowd rushing in with you﴾: this is a large crowd that has rushed into the Fire with you, meaning it entered the Fire in your company and alongside you. Al-iqtiham is undertaking hardship and entering into it, and al-qahmah is hardship. This is the report of the speech of the tyrants among themselves, meaning they say this. The intended meaning of "the crowd" is their followers, who rushed into misguidance with them, so they rush into the punishment with them. ﴿No welcome to them﴾: a supplication from them against their followers. One says to whom one prays for: "marhaban" (welcome), meaning: you have come to a spacious land, not a narrow one, or: your land has become spacious for you, a spaciousness. Then "la" (no) is placed before it in an evil supplication.

﴿To them﴾ is an explanation of those against whom the supplication is made. ﴿Indeed they will burn in the Fire﴾ is a reason for their deserving the supplication against them. Similar to it is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾. It was also said: ﴿this is a crowd rushing in with you﴾ is the speech of the keepers (of Hell) to the leaders of the disbelievers, concerning their followers. ﴿No welcome to them, indeed they will burn in the Fire﴾ is the speech of the leaders. It was also said: all of this is the speech of the keepers.

﴿They said﴾, meaning the followers: ﴿Rather, you—no welcome to you! You have brought this upon us﴾. They mean: the supplication you prayed against us, you are more deserving of it. They gave as the reason their saying: ﴿you brought it upon us﴾, and the pronoun refers to the punishment or to its burning. If you ask: what is the meaning of their bringing the punishment upon them? I say: what is brought forward is the evil deed. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning. That is for what your hands have sent forward﴾. But since the leaders were the cause of it through their misleading, and the punishment was their requital for it, it was said: "you brought it forward for us." So the leaders are made the ones who bring forward, and the requital is made the thing brought forward. Thus two metaphors are combined, because the doers are in reality the ones who bring it forward, not their leaders, and the deed is what is brought forward, not its requital.

If you ask: then what of the one who made His saying ﴿no welcome to them﴾ the speech of the keepers, and how does His saying ﴿rather, you—no welcome to you﴾ fit with it, when the addressees, namely their leaders, did not speak in a way that would be a reply to them? I say: it is as if it were said: this which the keepers prayed against us, you, O leaders, are more deserving of it than we are, because of your misleading us and your causing what we are in of punishment. This is sound, as when a people beautify some wrongdoing for another people, who then commit it, and it is said to those who beautified it: "May Allah disgrace these people! How evil is their deed!" Then the one who beautified it says to those who beautified it: "Rather, you are more deserving of disgrace than we are. Were it not for you, we would not have committed that."

They said, the followers also: ﴿so increase him in punishment, doubled﴾, meaning multiplied, and its meaning: having double. Similar to it is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, these are the ones who misled us, so give them a double punishment﴾. It is that He adds to his punishment the like of it, so that it becomes two punishments, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment﴾. [[His saying, Exalted is He: "They said: Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, increase him in punishment, doubled," and He said in another place: "Give them double the punishment, and curse them with a great curse," and the story is one. Ahmad said: in this there is evidence that the two doubles are two of one thing, contrary to whoever said otherwise, because in one place He said ﴿increase him in punishment, doubled﴾, and the intended meaning is: the like of his punishment, so they become two punishments. And in two places He said ﴿doubled﴾, and the intended meaning is: having two punishments.]] It was reported in the exegesis, "a punishment, doubled": snakes and serpents. [[His saying "it was reported in the exegesis ..." etc.: the wording of al-Khazin: Ibn Abbas said: snakes and serpents. (Ghunaymi)]].

And they said, the pronoun referring to the transgressors, "men" (rijālan), meaning the poor Muslims whom they did not regard and who were among the wicked, the base and the worthless, having no good in them and no benefit. This was also because they opposed their religion, so in their eyes they were wicked. ﴿Did we take them as objects of mockery?﴾ It is read with the form of a statement, making it a description of "men" (rijālan), like His words ﴿We used to count them among the wicked﴾. It is also read with the interrogative hamza (hamzat al-istifhām), in which case it is a denial directed at themselves and a rebuke of themselves [[His words "wa-ta'nīb lahā" (and a rebuke of themselves) mean: censure and blame. Related by al-Ṣiḥāḥ (the Ṣiḥāḥ lexicon). (ʿ)]] for mocking them.

His words ﴿Or have our eyes turned away from them?﴾ have two possible connections. The first is that it connects to their words "What is the matter with us?", meaning: why do we not see them in the Fire? As if they were not in it. Rather, our eyes have turned away from them so that we do not see them while they are in it. They divided their situation between being among the people of Paradise and being among the people of the Fire, but their place was hidden from them.

The second connection is to ﴿We took them as objects of mockery﴾. Here the interrogative "am" (أم) may be a connecting particle (muttaṣila), meaning: which of the two actions did we do, the mockery of them, or the scorn and belittling of them? And that our eyes were raised above them and passed over them, in the sense of denying both matters against themselves. It is reported from al-Ḥasan: "All of that they did: they took them as objects of mockery, and their eyes turned away from them in contempt for them." Or it may be a disconnecting particle (munqaṭiʿa), following the statement ﴿We took them as objects of mockery﴾, as a statement or as a question, like your saying: "Is it camels, or sheep?" (إنها إبل أم شاء) and "Is Zayd with you, or is ʿAmr with you?" (أزيد عندك أم عندك عمرو). You may also suppose that the interrogative hamza is elided for the one who reads without the hamza, since "am" indicates it, so the two readings do not differ, namely the affirming and the eliding of the interrogative hamza.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 38, verse 64:

"Indeed that" — that is, what We have related of them — "is certainly true, [and] they must speak of it." Then he explained what it is, saying: "It is the mutual disputing of the people of the Fire." It has also been read in the accusative, [making it] a description of "that," because demonstrative pronouns are described by generic nouns. If you ask: why was that called a "disputing"? I answer: their back-and-forth speech, and the questions and answers that pass between them, were likened to what passes between disputants of this kind. [Mahmud said: "If you ask why that was called a disputing, I answer: their back-and-forth speech, and the questions and answers passing between them, were likened to what passes between disputants of this kind, and because the saying of the leaders, 'No welcome to them,' and the saying of their followers, 'Rather, it is you — no welcome to you,' belongs to the category of disputing."] Ahmad said: This confirms that what came earlier, His saying "No welcome to them! Indeed they will burn in the Fire," is the speech of the arrogant disbelievers, and His saying "Rather, it is you — no welcome to you" is the speech of the followers. So the dispute on this interpretation arises from both sides, and thus the mutual disputing is realized. This is unlike those who said that the first is the speech of the keepers of Hell and the second is the speech of the followers, for on that reading the dispute would come from only one of the two groups. Therefore the first explanation is more plausible and more firmly established.

And because the saying of the leaders, "No welcome to them," and the saying of their followers, "Rather, it is you — no welcome to you," belongs to the category of disputing, the whole exchange was called a "disputing" on account of its including that.

Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of Makkah: "I am only a warner. I warn you of the punishment of Allah upon the polytheists, and I say to you: the religion of truth is the Oneness of Allah, and that one should believe that there is no god but Allah, ﴿the One, the Unrivaled, the Irresistible﴾ over everything, and that dominion and lordship belong to Him in the whole world. He is ﴿the Mighty﴾, who cannot be overcome when He punishes the disobedient, and He is, along with that, ﴿the Forgiving﴾ to the sins of whoever seeks refuge in Him." Or say to them: "I am only a warner to you, of what I know, and I warn you of a punishment from One who has these attributes, for one like Him deserves to be feared for His punishment just as He deserves to be hoped for in His reward."

Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of Makkah: "I am only a warner. I warn you of the punishment of Allah upon the polytheists, and I say to you: the religion of truth is the Oneness of Allah, and that one should believe that there is no god but Allah, ﴿the One, the Unrivaled, the Irresistible﴾ over everything, and that dominion and lordship belong to Him in the whole world. He is ﴿the Mighty﴾, who cannot be overcome when He punishes the disobedient, and He is, along with that, ﴿the Forgiving﴾ to the sins of whoever seeks refuge in Him." Or say to them: "I am only a warner to you, of what I know, and I warn you of a punishment from One who has these attributes, for one like Him deserves to be feared for His punishment just as He deserves to be hoped for in His reward."

Say, ﴿It is a momentous news﴾. That is, this which I have informed you of, that I am a messenger who warns, and that God is One with no partner, is a momentous news from which none turns away except a heedless person of extreme heedlessness.

Then he argues for the soundness of his prophethood: what he reports about the Highest Assembly (al-Mala' al-A'la) and their disputing is a matter of which he had never had any knowledge at all. Then he came to know it without following the path people take to learn what they do not know, which is taking from people of knowledge and reading books. So he knew that this had come about only through revelation from God. ﴿Say, "It is only revealed to me that I am only a plain warner."﴾ That is, "because I am only a warner." The meaning is: nothing is revealed to me except for the purpose of warning, so the lam has been omitted and the verb's effect reaches the object directly (the word is in the accusative case).

It is also permissible for the word to be in the nominative case, with the meaning: "Nothing is revealed to me except this, namely that I warn and deliver the message and do not go to excess in it." That is, I am commanded only with this matter alone, and there is nothing for me beyond it. The word *innama* has also been read with a kasra (*inna*), on the basis of direct quotation, meaning: "except this statement, namely that I say to you, 'I am only a plain warner,' and I claim nothing else."

It has been said that the momentous news is the story of Adam (peace be upon him) and the reporting of it without having heard it from anyone. It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas that it is the Qur'an, and from al-Hasan that it is the Day of Resurrection.

If you ask: to what does ﴿when they disputed﴾ (*idh yakhtasimun*) relate? The answer: it relates to an omitted element, because the meaning is: "I had no knowledge of the speech of the Highest Assembly at the time of their disputing." And ﴿when your Lord said﴾ (*idh qala*) is a substitute for ﴿when they disputed﴾.

If you ask: what is meant by the Highest Assembly? The answer: the people of the story, namely the angels, Adam, and Iblis, because they were in the heavens and the back-and-forth speech took place among them.

If you object: the back-and-forth speech was not among them, but between God Most High and them, since it was God who spoke to them and they who spoke to Him. So you are faced with one of two options. Either you say the Highest Assembly are these beings and the back-and-forth was among them, in which case it was not the disputing among them. Or you say the back-and-forth was between God and them, in which case you have made God part of the Highest Assembly. The answer: God's conversation was conducted through the intermediary of an angel, so the one actually conversing was the intermediary angel. Thus it is correct to say that the back-and-forth was among the angels, Adam, and Iblis, and they are the Highest Assembly. The intended meaning of *al-ikhtisam* (disputing) is the back-and-forth speech as explained above.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 38, verses 71–74:

If you ask: how is it correct that He says to them, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being (basharan)," when they did not know what a human being (al-bashar) is and had no prior acquaintance with it? I answer: its explanation is that He had said to them, "Indeed, I am going to create a creature whose attributes are such-and-such," but when He related it, He confined Himself to the name. ﴿So when I have proportioned him﴾: when I have completed his creation and made him balanced, ﴿and breathed into him of My spirit﴾: and given him life and made him sentient and breathing, ﴿then fall down in prostration﴾: then fall, prostrating themselves. "Kull" (all) is for encompassing, and "ajma'un" (all together) is for collectivity. Together, the two indicate that they prostrated, all of them to the last, so that not one angel remained without prostrating, and that they prostrated together at one time, not scattered over different times.

If you ask: how is prostration to other than God permissible? I answer: what is not permissible is prostration to other than God in the manner of worship. As for prostration in the manner of honor and reverence, reason does not reject it, unless God knows there is a corruption in it, in which case He forbids it.

If you ask: how did He make an exception of Iblis from the angels when he is from the jinn? **Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on Surah 38, verses 75–76**

If you ask: what is the meaning of His saying ﴿I created with My two hands﴾? I answer: We have already explained that a person with two hands performs most of his actions with them. So working with the two hands came to dominate all other actions that are performed without them, to the point that it is said of an action of the heart: "It is among what your two hands have done." And it is said of someone who has no hands: "Your two hands tied it shut (awkata) and your mouth blew on it." (Footnote: His saying "your two hands tied it shut" — in al-Sihah: awka 'ala ma fi siqa'ihi, meaning he tied shut the water-skin with its cord. (Ed.))

So there came to be no difference between your saying "This is something I did" and "This is something your two hands did." From the same usage is His saying ﴿of what Our hands have done﴾ (36:71) and ﴿for what I created with My two hands﴾.

If you ask: what is the meaning of His saying ﴿What prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands?﴾? I answer: The aspect for which Iblis found prostration to Adam objectionable, and which he disdained, was that it was prostration to a created being. He was overcome by his own self and was arrogant, refusing that his prostration should be to other than the Creator. Added to this, Adam was created from clay while he was created from fire, and he saw that fire has a superiority over clay. He thought it a grave matter to prostrate to a created being when he had a higher rank than him. He forgot that when God, glorified is He, commanded this, He commanded His most honoured servants and those nearest to Him in rank, namely the angels. They were more entitled to set aside their selves from humbling themselves before a lowly human, and to disdain prostrating to him, yet they did not do so. They obeyed God's command and kept it before their eyes, and they did not consider the disparity between the one who prostrates and the one to whom prostration is made, out of reverence for their Lord's command and glorification of His address. Therefore he (Iblis), despite his being lower than their ranks, should have been the more fitting to follow them and trace their path, and to know that their prostration to one lower than them was by God's command, or that they exerted themselves more than him in worship through prostration to Him, because of what it contains of abandoning pride and lowering the wing.

So it was said to him: "What prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands?" That is: what prevented you from prostrating to a thing which, as you say, is a created being that I fashioned with My hands (there is no doubt that it is created), in obedience to My command and in glorifying My address, as the angels did? So He mentioned to him what he had left off prostrating to, together with the reason he clung to in leaving it. And it was said to him: "Why did you leave it while this reason existed, when God had commanded you?" That is: it was incumbent upon you to regard God's command and not regard this reason. The example of this is: a king commands his vizier to visit some fallen-from-favour courtier, and he refuses out of regard for that man's fall. So the king says to him: "What prevented you from humbling yourself before one whose fall is not hidden from me?" He means: why did you not regard my command and my address, and leave off regarding his fall? And in it is: "I created him with My hands, so I know his state better, and despite that I commanded the angels to prostrate to him for a wise purpose that called Me to it: a bestowal of noble honour upon him and a trial for the angels. Who are you that you should turn yourself away from prostrating to him, when I did not turn Myself away from commanding prostration to him?"

It is said: the meaning of ﴿for what I created with My two hands﴾ is: for what I created without intermediary. It was read as "bi-yadayya" (with the ya' of the dual), as "bi-mishrakhiyy" is read. It was read as "biyadi" in the singular. ﴿Are you among the exalted?﴾ means: among those who have exalted themselves. He answered that he was among the exalted when he said ﴿I am better than him﴾ (38:76). It is also said: ﴿Have you become arrogant now, or have you always been among the arrogant since you were?﴾ The hamza (in the phrase) signifies a demand for affirmation (taqrir). It was read as "istakbarta" with the interrogative particle omitted, since "am" (or) indicates it. Or it is in the sense of a statement. This is on the principle of the more fitting: that is, had he been created from fire, he would not have prostrated to him, because he is a created being like myself, so how should I prostrate to one who is beneath me, since he is from clay and fire overcomes clay and consumes it? And the second clause, ﴿You created me from fire﴾, has taken the place of an appositive (ʿatf al-bayan) relative to the thing it follows, in clarification and explanation.

Actually, let me give you the translation directly:

"from it" — from Paradise. It was also said: from the heavens. It was also said: from the form (khilqah) in which you are, because he used to boast of his form, so God changed his form; he became black after having been white, ugly after having been beautiful, and darker after having been luminous. Al-rajim: the stoned, meaning the expelled, just as he is called al-madhur (the cast-out) and the accursed, because whoever is driven away is pelted with stones in his wake. Al-rajm: throwing stones. Or because the devils are pelted with shooting stars.

Rather, the meaning is: the curse is upon him in this world. When the Day of Judgment comes, the curse is joined to him by that which will make him forget the curse, so it is as if it has ended.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 38, verses 84–85:

It has been read as "fa-l-ḥaqqa wa-l-ḥaqqa" (فالحق والحق), with both in the accusative, on the basis that the first is an oath particle (muqsam bihi), like the phrase ﴿إن عليك الله أن تبايعا﴾ [meaning: "By God, it is incumbent upon you to pledge allegiance"]. Its answer (jawab) is ﴿لأملأن﴾ ("I will surely fill"). The phrase ﴿والحق أقول﴾ ("and the truth I say") is a parenthetical insertion (i'tiraḍ) between the oath-object and the thing sworn to, and its meaning is: "I say nothing but the truth." By "the truth" (al-ḥaqq) is meant either His name, may He be glorified and exalted, which is in His words ﴿أن الله هو الحق المبين﴾ ("that God is the manifest Truth"), or the truth which is the opposite of falsehood; God magnified it by swearing by it.

It has also been read with both in the nominative, on the basis that the first is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is omitted, like His words ﴿لعمرك﴾ ("by your life"), meaning: "So the truth is my oath: I will surely fill..." And "and the truth I say" means: "I say it," like His statement, "I did not do it" (kullahu lam asna'). It has also been read with both in the genitive, on the basis that the first is an oath-object with its particle of swearing omitted, like your saying: "Allah, I will surely do it."

"And the truth I say" may mean: "I say nothing but the truth," in the manner of quoting the wording of the one who swears by it. Its meaning is emphasis and intensification.

This reading is also permissible in the accusative and the nominative. It is a subtle and good reading. It has also been read with the first in the genitive and the second in the accusative. Its explanation, according to what we have mentioned, is: ﴿مِنْكَ﴾ ("from you") means from your kind, namely the devils; and ﴿وَمِمَّنْ تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ﴾ ("and whoever of them follows you") means from the offspring of Adam.

If you ask: ﴿أجمعين﴾ ("all") is emphasis for what? I say: it must emphasize either the pronoun in ﴿منهم﴾ or the kaf in ﴿منك﴾ together with ﴿من تبعك﴾. Its meaning is: "I will surely fill Hell with the followed and the followers, all of them, leaving none of them out." Or: "I will surely fill it with the devils and with whoever follows them from all mankind, with no difference between one people and another, since there are followers among them from the sons of the prophets and others."

﴿It is nothing but a reminder from God to the worlds﴾, to both humans and jinn. He revealed it to me, and I convey it.

From the Messenger of God (ﷺ), peace and blessings of God be upon him and his family: "The pretender has three signs: he competes with one above him, he reaches for what he cannot attain, and he says what he does not know."[[Narrated by al-Tha'labi through Muhammad ibn 'Awn, from Muhammad ibn al-Musalla, from Hayawa ibn Shurayh, from Arṭāt ibn al-Mundhir, from Damra ibn Habib, from Salama ibn Nufayl, as a marfu' report. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Shu'ab in the thirty-third section, from the narration of Baqiyya from Arṭāt, as a saying (of a companion). Abu Nu'aym narrated it from Wahb ibn Munabbih as a saying.]]

﴿And you will surely come to know its news﴾: that is, what will reach you at death, or on the Day of Resurrection, or at the time of the spread and dominance of Islam, concerning the truth of its report and that it is the truth and the sincere word. This contains a warning.

From the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surah Sad, God will give him ten good deeds for every mountain God subjected to David in weight, and will protect him from persisting in a sin, minor or major."[[Narrated by al-Tha'labi, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Wahidi, from a hadith of Ubayy, may God be pleased with him.]]
